Definition: (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops
BiblicalUsage: Aggaph means wings — the wings of an army, or crowds of troops — and it appears only in Ezekiel, always of armies in the day of judgment. God will scatter all who are around the prince 'to every wind,' and all his bands; the fugitives will fall by the sword with all their bands; and Gog's bands will fall on the mountains of Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: Troops scattering is the picture, and the word only counts the wings of the army — the judgment is the Lord's, not the noun's.
